title: Sheinbaum and AMLO Bid Farewell to Cárdenas: “He Was a Transformer” and “Indispensable Reference Point”
author: SinEmbargo Staff
content:
_This article by SinEmbargo Staff originally appeared in the[October 28, 2026
edition of SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4895329/csp-y-amlo-despiden-
a-cardenas-fue-un-transformador-y-referente-imprescindible/), an independent
Mexican digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, October 28 (SinEmbargo).-** [**President Claudia Sheinbaum
Pardo**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/claudia-sheinbaum/) (**CSP**) and
former President **Andrés Manuel López Obrador** (**AMLO**) mourned the death
of **Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas** , whom they described as a forerunner of the
**democratic movement** and as someone who transformed the political life of
**Mexico**.

The **Engineer died** this Wednesday, October 28, at **92 years of age** , and
after his passing a wave of messages arose from figures of all
[**parties**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/politica/) to express their
condolences and recognize his **legacy** in the political life of the country.

President Claudia Sheinbaum was one of the first to mourn his death with a
[message](https://x.com/Claudiashein/status/2115647058417693113) published on
her social networks, in which she highlighted that Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas was
"always faithful to the defense of national sovereignty and social causes. His
dignity and republican conviction remain an indispensable reference point for
our nation."

> "With deep sorrow we mourn the passing of Engineer Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas
> Solórzano, a man of firm principles, who transformed the political life of
> our country. His role in the contemporary history of Mexico is fundamental
> […]. Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano lives forever in the History of Mexico,"
> the head of the Executive posted.

![Screenshot of President Sheinbaum's message on X mourning Cuauhtémoc
Cárdenas](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/02-sheinbaum-message-cardenas.jpg)President Claudia
Sheinbaum mourned the death of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas. Photo: Screenshot from X
@Claudiashein

Former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador, who since his retirement from
political life has only been seen a couple of times, reappeared on social
media for the third time since 2018 to mourn the death of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas,
whom he called "a transformer."

> I send a hug to family, friends and compañeros for the regrettable passing
> of Engineer Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano, forerunner of the democratic
> movement in the recent history of Mexico. Without him, the political reality
> of the country would be different. He was a transformer; he leaves us his
> teachings and the ideals that never die.
>
> Andrés Manuel López Obrador

![Screenshot of López Obrador's message on X mourning Cuauhtémoc
Cárdenas](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/03-amlo-
message-cardenas.jpg)AMLO also highlighted the legacy of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas.
Photo: Screenshot from X @lopezobrador_

## Leaders of All Parties Mourn the Death of Cárdenas

The leaderships of all political parties also shared messages on their social
networks to recognize the legacy of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas as a reference point
of Mexican politics.

Ariadna Montiel, leader of Morena, highlighted in her post that the Engineer's
career "is part of the democratic memory of our nation."

> "His participation in the historic struggle of 1988 opened new paths for the
> Mexican left and contributed to transforming the political life of the
> country. His legacy is linked to the defense of the vote and the right of
> the people to freely decide their destiny. From the tradition of
> nationalism, he upheld fundamental causes of our history: sovereignty, the
> defense of the national patrimony and social justice," her message reads.

> [Post by @A_MontielR on
> X](https://twitter.com/A_MontielR/status/2115646515234349309)

> [Post by @alitomorenoc on
> X](https://twitter.com/alitomorenoc/status/2115639037675360752)

Also mourning the death of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas was Alejandro "Alito" Moreno,
leader of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), the party to which the
Engineer belonged and with which he broke to form the Party of the Democratic
Revolution (PRD).

> "I deeply regret the passing of Eng. Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano, an
> outstanding figure of Mexico's political life, whose career left an
> important mark on the democratic history of our country," the PRI leader
> posted.

Jorge Romero Hernández, leader of the National Action Party (PAN), also shared
a message in which he expressed his condolences for the death of the Engineer
and underscored his contribution to the struggle for democracy.

> "I deeply regret the passing of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano, a man who
> marked the history of Mexico and contributed to the struggle for democracy
> in our country. My condolences to his family and loved ones. Rest in peace,"
> he posted.

> [Post by @JorgeRoHe on
> X](https://twitter.com/JorgeRoHe/status/2115647563252568306)

Jorge Álvarez Máynez, leader of Movimiento Ciudadano, shared a series of
photographs on his Facebook account in which he appears alongside Cuauhtémoc
Cárdenas, with a message in which he said that "being a Cardenista is being on
the right side of history."

> "The history of the 20th century is the history of Lázaro and Cuauhtémoc:
> the struggle for economic equality and political equality. The struggle for
> democracy. Rest in peace," he posted.

The newly created party Somos, led by Guadalupe Acosta Naranjo, who was also
leader of the PRD, the party founded by Cárdenas Solórzano, mourned the
Engineer's death, asserting that "with his passing we all lose. Democracy
loses. Mexico loses."

> "Somos mourns the sad passing of Engineer Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano, a
> fundamental pillar of the construction of modern democracy in Mexico and a
> statesman who always knew how to put the interests of the country above any
> personal aspiration," reads its Facebook post.
